ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point L is at the lower left, LK is a horizontal ray from L to the right, and K is on the horizontal line; KM goes vertically upward from K to M, and there is a right-angle mark at K, indicating LK ⟂ KM. LM is the slanted line from L to M. There is also a slanted ray from L toward the upper right passing through J, JM connects J and M, and there is a right-angle mark at J, indicating LJ ⟂ JM. Segments JM and KM have the same tick marks, indicating JM = KM. Angle ∠JLM is labeled (6x+8)°, and angle ∠KLM is labeled (9x−4)°. Reasoning: Consider right triangles ΔLJM and ΔLKM. They both have LM as the hypotenuse and share the same hypotenuse LM; also because the figure marks JM = KM, the two right triangles satisfy that the hypotenuse and one leg are correspondingly equal, so by HL, ΔLJM ≅ ΔLKM can be obtained. Therefore their corresponding angles at point L are equal: ∠JLM = ∠KLM. Thus 6x+8 = 9x−4, solving gives 12 = 3x, so x = 4. The target angle ∠KLM = 9x−4 = 9(4)−4 = 32°.

raw_record.question_text: What is the measure of $\angle KLM$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: L is the left vertex, LK is a horizontal ray to K, KM is vertical, and LM is a diagonal segment. A second slanted ray from L passes through J, with segment JM drawn to M. The image marks right angles at J between LJ and JM and at K between LK and KM, and marks JM congruent to KM. The angle at L between LJ and LM is labeled (6x+8)°, while the target angle KLM, between KL and LM, is labeled (9x-4)°. Use the two right triangles ΔLJM and ΔLKM: they share hypotenuse LM, have one congruent leg JM = KM, and both are right triangles, so they are congruent by HL. Therefore their angles at L are equal, so 6x+8 = 9x-4. Solve x = 4, then ∠KLM = 9x-4 = 32°.
